title: Solid Context: Hierarchical Owner Graph Lookup Without Re-Render Propagation

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In React, updating a Context is like yelling through a megaphone: every single component in the building has to wake up and check if the message was for them. In SolidJS, Context is just a book placed on a shelf: children only look at the shelf when they first arrive. If they subscribe to a signal inside the book, only their private reading glasses light up when the text changes.
progressiveExplaining.junior: Solid's Context API is created using `createContext(defaultValue)` and consumed using `useContext(MyContext)`. You provide a value with `<MyContext.Provider value={...}>{children}</MyContext.Provider>`. Unlike React, **changing a Context Provider's value does NOT re-render intervening child components**, because Solid components run only once.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Solid Context operates on the static **Owner Tree** (`Owner` hierarchy) established at component initialization. `useContext` performs an `O(depth)` upward walk along `Owner._parent` pointers until it encounters an Owner containing a matching `context` key. When the provider value is a signal or store, child consumers bind directly to the signal itself, eliminating context-induced re-render waterfalls entirely.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When `<Context.Provider value={val}>` renders, Solid creates an internal `Owner` node whose `.context` dictionary stores `{ [Context.id]: val }`. When a descendant calls `useContext(Context)`, Solid reads `getOwner()`, loops `while (node) { if (node.context?.[id]) return node.context[id]; node = node._parent; }`, and returns the stored value (or default). Because no subscription to the provider node itself is established, context lookups have zero runtime invalidation cost.

rosettaStone.react: `createContext` + `useContext` (triggers re-render on all consumers when value reference changes).
rosettaStone.vue: `provide()` / `inject()` traversing the component instance parent chain.

codeComparison.title: React Context Re-render Cascade vs SolidJS Granular Context
codeComparison.summary: React Context forces all consumers and intermediate components to re-render; Solid Context links direct signal subscribers with zero intermediate work.

legacyOrBad.label: React Context Cascade
legacyOrBad.snippet: <ThemeContext.Provider value={theme}> // ❌ Re-renders all consumers on change

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if you pass a raw signal value `value={theme()}` instead of the signal accessor `value={theme}` to a Context Provider?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your understanding of Solid's run-once execution during Context provisioning.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Because the component body executing `<Context.Provider>` runs **only once**, passing `value={theme()}` resolves the signal immediately to its static initial string (e.g. `'light'`). Descendant components calling `useContext` will receive a static string that never updates. To pass reactive state through Context in Solid, you must pass the **signal accessor itself** (`value={theme}`) or a getter object (`value={{ get theme() { return theme(); } }}`).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Never call the signal getter `value={mySignal()}` inside the provider props; pass the accessor function `value={mySignal}`.

interviewGotchas.question: Can `useContext` be called inside an asynchronous callback (like `setTimeout` or after an `await`) in SolidJS?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of Owner tracking context loss across asynchronous boundaries.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. `useContext` relies on `getOwner()` to find the current active node in the Owner hierarchy. When execution crosses an asynchronous boundary (like `setTimeout` or after an `await`), the asynchronous task runs with `Owner === null`. `useContext` will fail to find the hierarchy and will return the default context value.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Always call `useContext()` synchronously at the top of your component or helper function, storing the reference before starting async operations.
